Issued at 246 AM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Early morning surface analysis indicates a warm front 
stretching southeast across the middle and lower Missouri River 
Valleys, which then becomes nearly stationary across far western
Kentucky. Farther to the east, high pressure was centered 
across the central and eastern Great Lakes region. GOES water 
vapor imagery continues to depict a negative-tilt short wave 
lifting slowly northeast across Kansas and Oklahoma. A broad 
region of low-level southerly return flow was noted ahead of 
this feature into the upper Midwest, where theta-E advection and
isentropic ascent atop the elevated warm frontal zone was 
resulting in a WNW-ESE band of showers from southwest MN to 
portions of our area.

Across northern IL/northwest IN, these showers were currently 
focused along/south of the I-80 corridor, with decreasing 
intensity with eastward extent away from the better southerly 
low-level jet and atop somewhat drier easterly low-level flow. 
The expectation is that these showers will continue to lift 
slowly north across the area this morning, though with some 
gradual weakening due to dampening of the approaching short wave
trough and an eastward translation of an upper jet streak over 
the Lakes to our northeast. This should result in decreasing 
shower coverage and intensity by this afternoon, although the 
presence of the elevated baroclinic zone and weak forcing within
a fairly moist thermodynamic profile will likely maintain some 
threat for at least isolated light showers at times into this 
evening. Overall however, afternoon and early evening conditions
should be fairly decent with cloudy skies, temperatures in the 
upper 50s/low 60s and light east-southeast winds.

On Sunday, a secondary short wave (currently over the TX/OK 
Panhandle region) is forecast to track into the region, 
increasing precipitation chances again mainly from the lower 
Ohio Valley into central IL/IN. There is quite a bit of spread 
in model guidance with how far north precipitation will spread, 
with NBM pops pretty minimal across the LOT forecast area. Have 
included some low-chance pops across our southern tier of CWA 
counties during the day for this however, in collaboration with 
WFOs ILX/IND. Can't completely rule out a shower or sprinkle 
farther north, though have not introduced pops north of roughly 
the U.S. 24 corridor at this time. 

Much farther to the west, a long-wave trough is progged to 
eventually consolidate from several disturbances off the west 
coast, including the current closed low off of the Pacific 
Northwest. Guidance is in reasonable agreement in brining the 
long-wave trough across the Rockies Sunday night with a 
deepening surface low near 1000 mb developing across the Plains 
of KS/NE. This is expected to induce increasing, broad southerly
low-level flow across the eastern Plains and Midwest Monday. 
Best moisture return and precipitation chances look to initially
be largely along/west of the Mississippi River, though a period
of warm advection induced showers appears possible into parts 
of northern IL/WI during the day. Current NBM pops appear too 
high especially over our eastern CWA Monday into Monday night, 
and have trimmed them a bit in our east but may see these 
decrease further with later runs.

Confidence then decreases moving into mid-week with the 
evolution of the upper trough, and the track/trends of the 
primary surface low. Global ensembles continue to show 
significant spread in the details of the evolution of the 
primary circulation within the upper trough (the former Pacific 
NW closed low) and the degree of phasing with a northern-stream 
disturbance dropping southeast across the Canadian Prairies. 
This has significant impacts on the track, intensity, location 
and potential occlusion of the primary surface low from Monday 
night onward. At this time it does appear that the early/mid- 
week period will be somewhat unsettled with chances of more 
widespread rain. Potentially windy and continued warmer than 
average conditions are also likely especially Monday into 
Tuesday. Of lowest confidence is perhaps how quickly the system 
departs mid-late week, and the magnitude of any intrusion of 
cooler air as it does.

Ratzer
